text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 40

The all-male panel is, on its own, weak evidence. It's common, often reflects who holds senior posts, and proves nothing about this decision. Don't build your case on it — it reads as an accusation of bias and invites a defensive response.

Your strong card is the qualification comparison: a master's in educational leadership and five years actually doing deputy-principal work versus unspecified "courses" and classroom years. That's a concrete, documentable gap, and in many jurisdictions it shifts the burden onto the employer to justify the choice.

So: send a firm written follow-up demanding the explanation you're legally entitled to, citing the qualification gap. Mention the panel's composition only as context, or hold it back. Consider consulting your union or an employment lawyer now.
